data.title: Undo
data.tagline: Undo rolls your last action back exactly as it was—Ctrl+Z brings the wrongly deleted row back, no retyping.
data.learningOutcome: You know undo restores the original state rather than recreating it, and that it cannot reach back past a page refresh.
data.description: Press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on Mac) to step backward, and redo to step forward again if you go too far. It has limits: usually only the last several steps, and the history is gone after refresh or close—important deletions still deserve a confirmation rather than relying on undo.

learning.assumes: You have pressed Ctrl+Z to undo typing in any editor.
learning.outcome: You know undo restores the original state rather than recreating it, and that it cannot reach back past a page refresh.

distinctions.label: Rollback
distinctions.explanation: Rollback reverts a whole version, like a deployment; Undo reverts your single last action.

distinctions.label: Popconfirm
distinctions.explanation: Popconfirm prevents a risky action before it happens; Undo rescues it right after.

explanation.title: The state before the action
explanation.text: Each step stores a "before" snapshot; pressing undo restores that original rather than regenerating it.

explanation.title: Paired with redo
explanation.text: Undo steps back, redo (Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y) re-applies the undone step. Both share one history.

explanation.title: History is finite
explanation.text: Usually only recent steps survive, and refresh or close clears it. Critical actions still deserve confirmation first.

data.boundary: Undo is not "recreate": it restores the original record, ID and timestamps included, while recreating makes a new one. It also differs from rollback, which reverts a whole version such as a deployment. The same applies to working with AI—"undo this step" beats "make a new one" on both speed and safety.

lessonPractice.title: You deleted the wrong quote row. Which way recovers it fastest and most safely?

options.label: Press Ctrl+Z right away to undo the delete
options.feedback: Correct. Undo rolls back the last step exactly as it was—faster than retyping and free of new mistakes.

options.label: Recreate an identical record from memory
options.feedback: Retyping creates a new record and risks misremembering; undo restores the original one.

options.label: Refresh the page to cancel the delete
options.feedback: Refreshing does not undo anything and may wipe the undo history—after that there is no way back.

data.agentPrompt: Add undo to the table's delete action: Ctrl+Z restores a wrongly deleted row exactly as it was. Keep the confirmation dialog before deleting as well.

references.title: Undo, redo and the history stack
